title: QBR - Helix AI Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage growth, cost trends, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is seeing increased inference volume from a new agent product; interested in a Dedicated capacity pilot and deeper cost optimization. Agreed next steps: send detailed usage + cost breakdown, schedule SE-led benchmark for peak traffic, and share security/compliance pack for VPC deployment.
topics: cost per 1k tokens and saving levers

transcript: 00:00 Maya (Redwood): All right, thanks everyone for joining. quick intro round and we'll jump into the QBR items.
00:12 Dana (Helix): Hi, Dana here, head of MLOps. Owen, Sofia and Ethan also with me. thanks for doing this.
00:20 Maya: Thanks. Maya Chen from Redwood, with Carlos Ruiz our SE and Priya Nambiar from CS. agenda: usage, costs, reliability, roadmap.
00:34 Carlos (Redwood): We'll start with the usage trends. we pulled the last 90 days and flagged a few spikes. note: auto-transcript may have small errors.
01:02 Maya: Dana, quick confirm: the spike last week was from the agent rollout right? saw 2.4x overall.
01:10 Dana: yes, new agent feature rolled out to 15% of users, ramping. peak QPS window is about 20:00 UTC, longer contexts too so tokens per call up ~30%.
01:28 Carlos: that matches our export. avg tokens per response moved from ~180 to ~240. that increases cost and affects batching behavior.
01:46 Owen: can you give cost per 1k tokens on our current hosted plan? we need to model unit economics versus internal endpoints.
01:54 Maya: currently you're at roughly $0.45 per 1k tokens across models in hosted. with Dedicated plus prefix caching and smarter batching we estimate down to $0.28 per 1k in your mix.
02:10 Dana: that's a meaningful delta. what's the latency tradeoff? our SLA goal is sub-200ms p95 for short responses.
02:18 Carlos: we recommend micro-batching for background traffic and preserve the low-latency path for p95-sensitive flows. also KV cache prefixing helps repeated prompts without adding latency.
02:36 Ethan (Helix): any quality risk with quantization? we saw some drift with q4_0 in dev tests.
02:44 Carlos: quality depends on model and task. we usually run a canary with your reranker and core chat, and our eval harness will surface regressions against your golden prompts.
03:05 Sofia (CTO): about Dedicated pilot, what does the onboarding look like and can we do a partial traffic cutover?

03:14 Priya (Redwood): onboarding is typically a week for configuration and baseline benchmarks. Carlos will run the bench and we can start with canary traffic or routing specific routes to Dedicated.
03:31 Carlos: for the bench we'll need your peak QPS window, sample payloads, and a small model bundle. we'll propose instance configs and a runbook.
03:48 Dana: Peak QPS details: about 1,200 rps at peak and spikes up to 1,800 for short bursts. we'll send exact window and RPS histogram.
04:02 Maya: perfect. on reliability, we logged two incidents this quarter; can you walk us through the region failover from July 11?
04:12 Ethan: sure, we saw degraded throughput for two hours during a provider region failover; some in-flight requests dropped and retries caused a small backlog.

04:24 Carlos: logs show failover triggered cross-region routing; retry storms are common. we recommended token-level backpressure and our automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model to keep latency stable.
04:40 Owen: are those fallback policies configurable per route? we have some sensitive flows where quality is paramount.
04:48 Carlos: yes, policy is per-route. you can define fallback model tiers, max retry windows, and circuit-breaker thresholds in the route config.
05:05 Maya: security and compliance question: you're exploring VPC/private deployment. let's cover requirements.
05:12 Dana: we need VPC peering, bring-your-own-KMS, SOC 2 type II, and audit logs retained for 12 months. also SAML SSO integration.
05:25 Priya: we have a security pack that covers SOC2/ISO, network diagrams and KMS integration guides. we'll share that after the call.
05:38 Owen: what about data residency? some customers require EU-only processing for certain datasets.
05:45 Maya: we can pin model serving to regions and enforce routing policies; for Private deployments you control the VPC and region.
05:56 Dana: great. on cost optimization, you mentioned caching and batching. any quick wins we can try on hosted while we evaluate Dedicated?

06:04 Carlos: yes: enable prefix KV caching for repeat prompts, enable adaptive batching on background workers, and use response-length targeting to route short responses to a low-latency optimized path. we can provide config snippets.
06:20 Sofia: timeline question: if we want Dedicated pilot, how long to get SLA-backed capacity?
06:27 Maya: pilot can start within 2-3 weeks, SLA typically kicks in for Reserved/Dedicated after contract and capacity provisioning, usually 4-6 weeks depending on region.
06:40 Dana: procurement will need pricing and T&Cs to review. can you send a pricing estimate for 6 months with projected ramp?
06:47 Maya: yes we'll include a cost model with hosted baseline, Dedicated pilot estimate and break-even analysis.
07:02 Ethan: about alerts and observability: we need token-level cost dashboards and per-route p95 latency alerts.
07:10 Priya: Redwood Console supports token and route breakdowns, and you can configure alerts and retention windows; we can give org-level access.
07:24 Owen: any recommended SLOs for a hybrid setup? we want to keep customer-facing latency tight but use cheaper routes for async processing.
07:32 Carlos: common pattern: 200ms p95 for interactive routes, 500-1000ms for async. use route-based failovers and circuit breakers to preserve p95.
07:48 Dana: curious about routing by cost. can Redwood route requests to lower-cost model during off-peak automatically?
07:55 Maya: yes, smart routing policies can route by time-of-day, cost budget, or degradation; we can configure fallbacks to cheaper model variants.
08:08 Sofia: on the product roadmap, are there upcoming features relevant to us? better on-prem support and longer-context kernels?
08:14 Carlos: roadmap items this quarter include longer-context kernel optimizations, improved KV cache heuristics, and expanded quant profiles for quality-preserving compression.
08:26 Dana: good to hear. can we get early access to the longer-context optimizations? we have a couple of evaluation prompts.
08:34 Carlos: yes we can arrange an early test with your dataset; we'll coordinate offline.
08:44 Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners before we wrap.
08:50 Dana: quick note the transcript sometimes munges product names; send the raw exports if possible.

09:00 Maya: noted. recap: Maya will send 90-day usage export and cost breakdown; Carlos will schedule Dedicated benchmark and runbook; Priya to send security pack and diagrams; Dana/Owen to supply peak windows and success criteria.
09:18 Owen: we'll send peak hist and CIDR info by next Tue. procurement will review pricing and come back with questions.
09:26 Priya: I'll share the SOC2 and KMS guides and an onboarding checklist.
09:34 Maya: any other blockers from Helix side?
09:38 Dana: none at the moment, just need internal approvals.
09:42 Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with attachments and set the pilot kickoff for the week of 2026-09-28 assuming approvals.
note: transcript has occasional auto-transcription artifacts such as 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' and minor name mismatches; please reference recordings for verbatim quotes.
